content:
support-jess: FYI customer LumenPay is seeing p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate starting ~03:20 UTC. They report latency jumps during long chat sessions. I pulled telemetry — KV miss rate for tenant t-lumen is ~39% vs normal ~2%. Posting traces and a few request-IDs.

support-jess: Logs snippets:
```
req=01FZQ4A req_id=xyz-1 tenant=t-lumen model=redwood-v1 len=512 kv_cache.hit=123 kv_cache.miss=80 miss_rate=0.39 prefix_miss=0.41 prefix_entropy=0.88
req=01FZQ4B req_id=xyz-2 tenant=t-lumen model=redwood-v1 len=480 kv_cache.hit=120 kv_cache.miss=95 miss_rate=0.44 prefix_miss=0.47 prefix_entropy=0.91
```

ara: Thanks Jess. Which branch of the runtime is serving them (hosted vs dedicated)? Any recent config changes for prefix keys?

support-jess: Hosted (prod-us-east). No config changes logged for that tenant in the last 72h. Customer says they started a new chat session orchestration yesterday; sessions include a per-message header X-Client-Session that looks like a UUID.

lee: That header could be part of the cache key if we include all headers in prefix fingerprint. Quick check: our cache key template for prefixes is: `prefix_key = tenant + ':' + model + ':' + route + ':' + headers_hash`. If headers_hash includes session IDs, cardinality explodes -> warmup + eviction thrash.

ara: Can you repro locally on staging with a load that rotates X-Client-Session per request?

lee: Yes. Repro steps I used:
```bash
for i in {1..400}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Session: $(uuidgen)" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://staging.api.redwood/infer &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
With that load, p95 jumps from ~80ms -> 380ms, and prefix_entropy per-shard goes to >0.8.

sam: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Normalize headers used in prefix hashing to a whitelist (drop X-Client-Session), 2) Temporarily bump max_prefix_entries for t-lumen to reduce eviction churn, 3) Add a tenant-specific prefix-pin for the hot conversation. Which is fastest?

lee: I can land a small hotfix to normalize header list in the key builder. Patch ready: `runtime/kv/key_builder: drop_headers = ["x-client-session"]` — will roll to canary. That should collapse cardinality immediately.

ara: Deploy plan: canary to 3 nodes for 10 minutes, monitor prefix_entropy and p95 for t-lumen, then continue to 20% if stable. Sam, can you approve the runtime config change and note a temporary bump for max_entries?

sam: Approved. Also enabling tenant cache bump: `tenant.t-lumen.kv.max_prefix_entries=50000` for 1 hour via runtime-config. I'll revert after stabilization.

lee: deploy-bot: Started rollout runtime-key-normalize to eng-runtime-canary (3 nodes) — build sha: ab12cd3.

deploy-bot: Rollout step 1/3 complete.

oncall-bot: Alert: t-lumen p95 decreased from 410ms -> 95ms within 8m of canary. Prefix_entropy dropped from 0.89 -> 0.12.

maria: Great. Please make a follow-up postmortem and add a runbook entry: how to detect header-driven key-cardinality and emergency mitigations (prefix whitelist, tenant pin, entries bump, circuit-breaker). Also add an automated monitor for sudden prefix_entropy > 0.2 per tenant (trigger paging).

support-jess: Customer confirms latency back to normal. I'm sending a summary and will keep ticket open until postmortem is in.

ara: P0 root cause: header-inclusion in prefix hashing allowed ephemeral session IDs to inflate prefix cardinality -> cache thrash and evictions -> cold starts for KV -> p95/p99 regressions. Action items: 1) ship key-builder header whitelist (merged), 2) add telemetry baseline for prefix_entropy per-tenant, 3) update SDK docs to call out not to surface per-message session IDs as cache-affecting headers, 4) create rollback plan for runtime knobs.

sam: I'll schedule a short oncall rotation to monitor t-lumen for 24h and then revert the max_prefix_entries bump.

support-jess: Thanks everyone. Marking as resolved in support tracker after PM posted.
